name: Cron library test gap
description: A cron expression library with decent code but only a handful of shallow tests; the agent must write a regression suite strong enough to catch behavioural bugs in every module.
taskPrompt: The `cronkit` library parses five-field cron expressions and computes upcoming run times, but its test suite (test/cron.test.js) only covers a few happy paths. We are about to hand this library to a new maintainer and want a regression suite that would catch any accidental behaviour change. Add tests under test/ (new files are fine, using node:test and node:assert) that thoroughly pin down the current behaviour of every module: field expansion, expression parsing and aliases, matching, next-run search and the upcoming list. Pay particular attention to boundaries, error handling and the documented rules in the README. Do not change anything under src/: the tests must pass against the current implementation, be deterministic (everything is UTC, no real clock) and run in under a few seconds with `node --test`.
visibleAcceptance: All new tests pass against the unmodified implementation and run with `node --test`
Each exported function has tests for normal use, boundary values and invalid input
The documented day-of-month/day-of-week rule, name handling and aliases are covered
Tests are deterministic, use no real clock or network, and src/ is untouched
